```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Merali 2024 developed two exposure-response (E-R) models for the
echocardiographic endpoints that guide mavacamten dose titration in
hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM): the Valsalva left ventricular outflow tract
gradient (VLVOTg, efficacy) and the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF,
safety). Both are driven by Cavg168, the average mavacamten plasma
concentration over the week before the echocardiogram. The paper then linked
them to the sponsor population PK model to compare dose-titration regimens;
that PK model is packaged as `Chang_2024_mavacamten`.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Merali_2024_mavacamten_lvot_gradient_valsalva"))$reference`
* Efficacy model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Merali_2024_mavacamten_lvot_gradient_valsalva"))$description`
* Safety model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Merali_2024_mavacamten_lvef"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13138> (open access)

The two models are separate files because the authors fitted them
separately, to different analysis sets.

# Population

The VLVOTg model was fitted to 3597 observations from 272 patients with
obstructive HCM in PIONEER-HCM, EXPLORER-HCM, PIONEER-OLE and the EXPLORER-LTE
cohort of MAVA-LTE. The LVEF model was fitted to 4175 observations from 331
patients: the same 272 patients with obstructive HCM plus 59 patients with
nonobstructive HCM from MAVERICK-HCM. Baseline covariates (Table S2): LVEF
mean 74% (SD 5.9) and 73% (6.4), VLVOTg mean 75.1 mmHg (34.0) and 63.5 (39.7),
40.8% and 43.5% female, about three quarters on a beta-blocker, NYHA class II
in about 72%. Patients who continued from a parent study into an extension had
their baseline values reset for the extension. Age and body weight are not
reported for the analysis sets.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Merali_2024_mavacamten_lvef")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `VLVOTg = VLVOTg0 * PBO(t) * exp(-kMAVA * Cavg168)` | -- | Results, first equation |
| `PBO(t) = PBOMAX + (1 - PBOMAX) * exp(-kPBO * t)` | -- | Results, second equation |
| `lrbase` (log VLVOTg0, ref.) | 4.22 | Table 2, 'Log(VLVOTg0.REF), log(mm Hg)' |
| `e_lvot_gradient_valsalva_bl_rbase` | 0.521 | Table 2, 'Log(VLVOTg0) ~ log(VLVOTg0/69)' |
| `e_ntprobnp_rbase` | 0.108 | Table 2, 'Log(VLVOTg0) ~ log(NT-proBNP/736)' |
| `lslope` (log kMAVA, ref.) | -5.66 | Table 2, 'Log(kMAVA.REF), log(1/(ng/mL))' |
| `e_lvot_gradient_valsalva_bl_slope` | 0.438 | Table 2, 'Log(kMAVA) ~ log(VLVOTg0/69)' |
| `lkpbo` | log(0.0373 /week) | Table 2, 'kPBO, 1/wk' |
| `pbomax` | 0.8767 (fixed) | Table 2, 'VLVOTgPBOMAX', and footnote |
| `etalrbase`, `etalslope` | 24.5%, 43.3% CV; r = 0.010 | Table 2, IIV rows |
| `expSd_lvot_gradient_valsalva` | 0.468 | Table 2, 'Residual SD (exponential error)' |
| `LVEF = LVEF0 * (1 - kMAVA * Cavg168^qq)` | -- | Results, third equation |
| `lrbase` (LVEF0, ref.) | log(74.0) | Table 2, 'LVEF0.REF, %' |
| `e_lvef_bl_rbase` | 33.6 / 100 | Table 2, 'LVEF0 ~ log(LVEF0/74), %' |
| `e_dis_hcm_nonobstructive_rbase` | -3.24 / 100 | Table 2, 'LVEF0 ~ nonobstructive HCM, %' |
| `e_sexf_rbase` | 1.40 / 100 | Table 2, 'LVEF0 ~ female, %' |
| `lslope` (log kMAVA, ref.) | -12.8 | Table 2, 'Log(kMAVA.REF), 1/(ng/mL)' |
| `e_study_explorerhcm_slope` | 4.29 | Table 2, 'Log(kMAVA.REF) ~ all studies except EXPLORER-HCM' |
| `e_lvef_bl_slope` | 1.73 | Table 2, 'Log(kMAVA.REF) ~ log(LVEF0/74)' |
| `pow` (qq, ref.) | 1.69 | Table 2, 'qqREF' |
| `e_study_explorerhcm_pow` | -0.64 | Table 2, 'qqREF ~ all studies except EXPLORER-HCM' |
| `etalrbase`, `etalslope` | SD 2.38 / 100; 61.6% CV; r = -0.062 | Table 2, IIV rows |
| `expSd_lvef` | 4.80 / 100 | Table 2, 'Residual SD' |
| Reference patient | VLVOTg 69 mmHg, NT-proBNP 736 ng/L; male EXPLORER-HCM patient with obstructive HCM, LVEF 74% | Table 2 footnote |

# Reference-patient exposure-response curves

With the random effects removed, the efficacy model at a long time after
baseline (placebo effect fully developed) and the safety model are evaluated
over a grid of Cavg168 values for the reference patients. For the LVEF model
the curve is drawn for EXPLORER-HCM and for the other studies, whose
exposure-response differs (Table 2).

```{r reference-curves, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
mod_vlvotg <- readModelDb("Merali_2024_mavacamten_lvot_gradient_valsalva")
mod_lvef <- readModelDb("Merali_2024_mavacamten_lvef")

cav_grid <- seq(0, 1000, by = 25)
ref_vlvotg <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = 1000, evid = 0L, CAV = cav_grid,
  LVOT_GRADIENT_VALSALVA_BL = 69, NTPROBNP = 0.736
)
ref_lvef <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  STUDY_EXPLORERHCM = c(1, 0), CAV = cav_grid
) |>
  mutate(
    id = 1L, evid = 0L,
    LVEF_BL = 74, DIS_HCM_NONOBSTRUCTIVE = 0, SEXF = 0
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(STUDY_EXPLORERHCM), CAV) |>
  mutate(time = seq_len(n())) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Time does not enter the LVEF model, so the whole grid is one typical patient
# observed at successive nominal times; the efficacy grid sits at week 1000,
# where the placebo effect has reached PBOMAX.
ref_vlvotg$time <- 1000 + seq_len(nrow(ref_vlvotg)) * 1e-6

sim_ref_v <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_vlvotg), ref_vlvotg, keep = "CAV") |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_ref_l <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_lvef), ref_lvef,
  keep = c("CAV", "STUDY_EXPLORERHCM")
) |>
  as.data.frame()

p1 <- ggplot(sim_ref_v, aes(CAV, lvot_gradient_valsalva)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 30, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Cavg168 (ng/mL)", y = "Valsalva LVOT gradient (mmHg)",
       title = "Efficacy (reference patient, steady placebo effect)")
p2 <- ggplot(sim_ref_l, aes(CAV, lvef,
  linetype = ifelse(STUDY_EXPLORERHCM == 1, "EXPLORER-HCM", "Other studies"))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "Cavg168 (ng/mL)", y = "LVEF (%)", linetype = NULL,
       title = "Safety (reference patient)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(p1)
print(p2)
```

## Closed-form and placebo checks

The paper states that the placebo effect "accounted for a maximum of 12.3%
decline in VLVOTg from baseline", i.e. `1 - PBOMAX`. The model output for the
reference patient is also recomputed from the Table 2 values directly.

```{r closed-form}
closed_v <- exp(4.22) * 0.8767 * exp(-exp(-5.66) * cav_grid)
closed_l_explorer <- 74 * (1 - exp(-12.8) * cav_grid^1.69)
closed_l_other <- 74 * (1 - exp(-12.8 + 4.29) * cav_grid^(1.69 - 0.64))

placebo_decline_pct <- 100 * (1 - sim_ref_v$lvot_gradient_valsalva[1] / exp(4.22))

checks <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "Maximum placebo decline in VLVOTg (%)",
    "VLVOTg at Cavg168 = 400 ng/mL (mmHg)",
    "LVEF at Cavg168 = 400 ng/mL, EXPLORER-HCM (%)",
    "LVEF at Cavg168 = 400 ng/mL, other studies (%)"
  ),
  Model = c(
    placebo_decline_pct,
    sim_ref_v$lvot_gradient_valsalva[sim_ref_v$CAV == 400],
    sim_ref_l$lvef[sim_ref_l$CAV == 400 & sim_ref_l$STUDY_EXPLORERHCM == 1],
    sim_ref_l$lvef[sim_ref_l$CAV == 400 & sim_ref_l$STUDY_EXPLORERHCM == 0]
  ),
  Reference = c(
    12.3,
    closed_v[cav_grid == 400],
    closed_l_explorer[cav_grid == 400],
    closed_l_other[cav_grid == 400]
  )
)
checks |>
  mutate(across(c(Model, Reference), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value model output against the paper's statement and the Table 2 closed form.")

# Same parameters on both sides (model vs. hand formula): differences are
# floating-point only. The placebo statement is printed to 3 figures.
stopifnot(
  abs(placebo_decline_pct - 12.3) < 0.05,
  all(abs(sim_ref_v$lvot_gradient_valsalva - closed_v) < 1e-6 * closed_v),
  all(abs(sim_ref_l$lvef[sim_ref_l$STUDY_EXPLORERHCM == 1] - closed_l_explorer) < 1e-6),
  all(abs(sim_ref_l$lvef[sim_ref_l$STUDY_EXPLORERHCM == 0] - closed_l_other) < 1e-6)
)
```

## Covariate effects on the baseline parameters

```{r covariate-effects}
th_v <- rxode2::rxode(mod_vlvotg)$theta
th_l <- rxode2::rxode(mod_lvef)$theta
cov_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Parameter, ~Contrast, ~Ratio,
  "VLVOTg0", "baseline VLVOTg 40 vs 69 mmHg", (40 / 69)^th_v[["e_lvot_gradient_valsalva_bl_rbase"]],
  "VLVOTg0", "baseline VLVOTg 120 vs 69 mmHg", (120 / 69)^th_v[["e_lvot_gradient_valsalva_bl_rbase"]],
  "VLVOTg0", "NT-proBNP 3000 vs 736 ng/L", (3 / 0.736)^th_v[["e_ntprobnp_rbase"]],
  "kMAVA (VLVOTg)", "baseline VLVOTg 120 vs 69 mmHg", (120 / 69)^th_v[["e_lvot_gradient_valsalva_bl_slope"]],
  "LVEF0", "baseline LVEF 60 vs 74%", (60 / 74)^th_l[["e_lvef_bl_rbase"]],
  "LVEF0", "nonobstructive vs obstructive HCM", exp(th_l[["e_dis_hcm_nonobstructive_rbase"]]),
  "LVEF0", "female vs male", exp(th_l[["e_sexf_rbase"]]),
  "kMAVA (LVEF)", "baseline LVEF 60 vs 74%", (60 / 74)^th_l[["e_lvef_bl_slope"]],
  "kMAVA (LVEF)", "other studies vs EXPLORER-HCM", exp(th_l[["e_study_explorerhcm_slope"]])
)
cov_tab |>
  mutate(Ratio = signif(Ratio, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value ratios implied by the Table 2 covariate effects.")
```

A patient with a lower observed baseline LVEF starts from a lower LVEF0 and
also has a smaller kMAVA, so the relative LVEF reduction at a given exposure
is smaller.

# Linking to the PK model: the first four weeks

All the regimens Merali 2024 simulated start at 5 mg once daily, and the first
titration decision is at week 4, so up to week 4 every regimen is the same
and Table S3 (VLVOTg below 30 mmHg) and Table S4 (LVEF below 50%) report one
value for all of them: 49.7% and 0.325% of 4000 virtual patients. Table 4
(5000 patients, representative CYP2C19 distribution) gives 50.8% and 0.2%.

This section rebuilds that week-4 snapshot for 200 virtual EXPLORER-HCM
patients: mavacamten 5 mg once daily for 4 weeks with
`Chang_2024_mavacamten`, Cavg168 from PKNCA over the last week (hours 504 to
672), then both E-R models at week 4 with their random effects and residual
error, as in the paper's simulations.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240501)
n_pat <- 200L

# CYP2C19 phenotype distribution of Table S1 (representative US / EU)
pheno_levels <- c("PM", "IM", "NM", "RM", "UM")
pheno_prob <- c(4.0, 20.9, 49.3, 22.8, 3.0) / 100

cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_pat),
  phenotype = factor(sample(pheno_levels, n_pat, replace = TRUE, prob = pheno_prob),
    levels = pheno_levels),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pat, 81.1, 16.9), 45), 150),
  CRCL = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pat, 94.5, 18), 30), 150),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_pat, 1, 0.408),
  # Table S2 VLVOTg-set baseline gradient, mean 75.1 (SD 34.0) mmHg, log-normal
  LVOT_GRADIENT_VALSALVA_BL = rlnorm(n_pat, log(75.1) - 0.5 * log(1 + (34 / 75.1)^2),
    sqrt(log(1 + (34 / 75.1)^2))),
  # Table S2 baseline LVEF, mean 74% (SD 5.9); EXPLORER-HCM enrolled LVEF >= 55%
  LVEF_BL = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pat, 74, 5.9), 55), 90),
  # NT-proBNP in ng/mL, log-normal around the 736 ng/L reference (spread assumed)
  NTPROBNP = rlnorm(n_pat, log(0.736), 1)
) |>
  mutate(
    CYP2C19_PM = as.integer(phenotype == "PM"),
    CYP2C19_IM = as.integer(phenotype == "IM"),
    CYP2C19_RM = as.integer(phenotype == "RM"),
    CYP2C19_UM = as.integer(phenotype == "UM"),
    CYP2C19_MISSING = 0L, DIS_HEALTHY = 0L, FED = 0L, FORM_SOLUTION = 0L,
    CONMED_OMEPRAZOLE = 0L, CONMED_ESOMEPRAZOLE = 0L, STUDY_MYK461014 = 0L,
    DOSE_MAVACAMTEN_MG = 5,
    STUDY_EXPLORERHCM = 1L, DIS_HCM_NONOBSTRUCTIVE = 0L
  )

pk_cov <- c("WT", "CRCL", "SEXF", "CYP2C19_PM", "CYP2C19_IM", "CYP2C19_RM",
  "CYP2C19_UM", "CYP2C19_MISSING", "DIS_HEALTHY", "FED", "FORM_SOLUTION",
  "CONMED_OMEPRAZOLE", "CONMED_ESOMEPRAZOLE", "STUDY_MYK461014", "DOSE_MAVACAMTEN_MG")

dose_rows <- cohort |>
  select(id, all_of(pk_cov)) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(0, 27 * 24, by = 24)) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 5, cmt = "depot")
obs_rows <- cohort |>
  select(id, all_of(pk_cov)) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(504, 672, by = 2)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
pk_events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, everything()) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r pk-simulate}
mod_pk <- readModelDb("Chang_2024_mavacamten")
sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = pk_events) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, phenotype), by = "id")
```

## PKNCA: Cavg168 at week 4

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, phenotype)
nca_dose <- pk_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, phenotype), by = "id")

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | phenotype + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | phenotype + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 504, end = 672, cav = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

cavg168 <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  select(id, phenotype, CAV = PPORRES)

cavg168 |>
  group_by(phenotype) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    median = signif(median(CAV), 3),
    p05 = signif(quantile(CAV, 0.05), 3),
    p95 = signif(quantile(CAV, 0.95), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(
    "CYP2C19 phenotype" = phenotype,
    "N" = n,
    "Median Cavg168 (ng/mL)" = median,
    "5th percentile" = p05,
    "95th percentile" = p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated Cavg168 over week 4 of mavacamten 5 mg once daily.")
```

## Echocardiographic endpoints at week 4

```{r er-week4}
er_events <- cohort |>
  left_join(cavg168 |> select(id, CAV), by = "id") |>
  mutate(time = 4, evid = 0L) |>
  select(id, time, evid, CAV, LVOT_GRADIENT_VALSALVA_BL, NTPROBNP, LVEF_BL,
    SEXF, DIS_HCM_NONOBSTRUCTIVE, STUDY_EXPLORERHCM) |>
  as.data.frame()

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240502)
sim_v4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_vlvotg, er_events,
  keep = c("CAV", "LVOT_GRADIENT_VALSALVA_BL")) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_l4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_lvef, er_events, keep = c("CAV", "LVEF_BL")) |>
  as.data.frame()

week4 <- data.frame(
  Endpoint = c("VLVOTg < 30 mmHg (%)", "LVEF < 50% (%)"),
  Simulated = c(100 * mean(sim_v4$sim < 30), 100 * mean(sim_l4$sim < 50)),
  `Table S3 / S4` = c(49.7, 0.325),
  `Table 4` = c(50.8, 0.2),
  check.names = FALSE
)
week4 |>
  mutate(Simulated = round(Simulated, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Week-4 proportions: 200 simulated patients against the paper's 4000- and 5000-patient simulations.")

stopifnot(
  # 200 patients give a binomial SE of about 3.5 points on a 50% proportion,
  # and the baseline-gradient distribution is an approximation (see below);
  # a mis-transcribed kMAVA, VLVOTg0 or residual SD moves this by tens of
  # points.
  abs(week4$Simulated[1] - 49.7) < 15,
  # LVEF below 50% is a ~0.3% event: assert only that it stays rare.
  week4$Simulated[2] < 5
)
```

The simulated change from baseline against Cavg168 has the shape of Figure 1:
VLVOTg falls steeply over the 5 mg exposure range while LVEF changes by a few
points.

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
fig1 <- bind_rows(
  sim_v4 |> transmute(CAV, cfb = LVOT_GRADIENT_VALSALVA_BL - sim,
    endpoint = "(a) Baseline VLVOTg - VLVOTg (mmHg)"),
  sim_l4 |> transmute(CAV, cfb = LVEF_BL - sim,
    endpoint = "(b) Baseline LVEF - LVEF (%)")
)
ggplot(fig1, aes(CAV, cfb)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Cavg168 (ng/mL)", y = "Change from baseline",
       caption = "Simulated analogue of Merali 2024 Figure 1 (week 4, 5 mg once daily).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Scale of the LVEF '%' rows.** The Results state that the LVEF model has
  log-normal random effects on LVEF0 and kMAVA and a log-normal residual
  error. Table 2 prints the LVEF0 covariate effects (33.6, -3.24, 1.40), the
  LVEF0 random-effect SD (2.38) and the residual SD (4.80) with a '%' label
  and no 'Log(...)' prefix. The maintainers read these as log-scale
  quantities multiplied by 100, so they are divided by 100 here: the baseline
  LVEF effect is a power exponent of 0.336, the nonobstructive-HCM and female
  effects shift log LVEF0 by -0.0324 and +0.0140, and the IIV and residual
  SDs are 0.0238 and 0.048 on the log scale. The 2025 refit of the same model
  with added Chinese patients (doi:10.1002/psp4.13312) reports its baseline
  LVEF exponent unscaled as 0.315, the same magnitude as 0.336. Read instead
  as additive percentage points, the residual SD would be 4.80 points rather
  than about 3.6 points at an LVEF of 74%.
- **IIV conversion.** The %CV rows are converted with omega^2 =
  log(1 + CV^2); the paper does not define its %CV. Covariances are
  r * omega_i * omega_j.
- **Baseline covariates are observed values.** In the Table 2 covariate rows
  'VLVOTg0' and 'LVEF0' denote the patient's observed baseline (Methods:
  "baseline VLVOTg on both VLVOTg0 and kMAVA"), supplied as
  `LVOT_GRADIENT_VALSALVA_BL` and `LVEF_BL`; the model parameters VLVOTg0 and
  LVEF0 carry their own random effects.
- **Baseline LVEF covariate on kMAVA.** The Results text says baseline LVEF
  acts on "the steepness parameter"; Table 2 places it on log kMAVA, which
  the model follows.
- **NT-proBNP unit.** The Table 2 footnote gives the reference as
  "736 ng/mL", but Table S2 reports NT-proBNP in ng/L (mean 1280), so the
  reference is 736 ng/L = 0.736 ng/mL and `NTPROBNP` is supplied in ng/mL.
- **Study effect.** "All studies except EXPLORER-HCM" is coded as
  `1 - STUDY_EXPLORERHCM`; extension records of patients who came from
  EXPLORER-HCM (the EXPLORER-LTE cohort of MAVA-LTE) carry
  `STUDY_EXPLORERHCM = 0`. Simulations of the approved regimen, as in the
  paper, use the EXPLORER-HCM value.
- **Placebo time.** `t` is time in weeks from the patient's (possibly reset)
  baseline; the placebo time course multiplies the gradient for mavacamten and
  placebo patients alike.
- **Virtual cohort.** Body weight and eGFR follow the Chang 2024 PK
  population (the E-R analysis sets do not report them); baseline VLVOTg and
  LVEF follow the Table S2 means and SDs (log-normal and truncated normal,
  LVEF at least 55% per the EXPLORER-HCM entry criterion). Table S2 prints
  the NT-proBNP SD as 34 against a mean of 1280 ng/L, which is not usable, so
  NT-proBNP is drawn log-normally around the 736 ng/L reference with a
  log-scale SD of 1; its exponent (0.108) makes the week-4 result insensitive
  to that choice. The paper resampled the observed EXPLORER-HCM patients
  instead.
- **Titration simulations not reproduced.** Tables 3, 4 and S3-S6 and
  Figures 2-3 come from 4000- and 5000-patient simulations of the
  concentration- and echocardiography-guided titration rules of Table 1 over
  40 and 104 weeks. Only the week-4 snapshot, before any titration step, is
  rebuilt here.
- **No erratum** for Merali 2024 was found on Europe PMC (checked
  2026-10-31).
